title: China’s humanoid robots have been taking over the global market. Now the US is banning them
facts: The Trump Administration banned new humanoid and quadruped robot imports from foreign manufacturers.
The US import ban covers power converters used to connect renewable energy infrastructure to the power grid.
The US Federal Communications Commission determined that internet-connected foreign robots pose supply chain and cybersecurity risks.
China's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning stated Beijing's opposition to US national security restrictions.
The US Federal Communications Commission previously banned foreign-made drones in December.
China's humanoid robot sector comprises more than 140 manufacturing companies.
A LexisNexis report showed six of the world's top ten humanoid robot startups ranked by patent strength are Chinese.
Figure AI is a humanoid robotics company based in San Jose, California.
Chinese companies accounted for 90% of global humanoid robot shipments last year.
The United States was the largest overseas market for Chinese-made humanoid robots last year according to Interact Analysis.
US technology firm Nvidia announced a research partnership with Chinese robot maker Unitree.
The US Department of Defense barred Unitree from defense contracts over alleged Chinese military ties.
Soumen Mandal serves as principal analyst at Counterpoint Research.
Lian Jye Su serves as chief analyst specializing in AI and humanoid robots at Omdia.
Agile Robots is a robotics company based in Germany.
